newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong starts huge transfer of Viet boatpeople.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong starts huge transfer of Viet boatpeople.

text.p: Hong Kong set in motion its biggest mass transfer of Vietnamese boatpeople on Monday when police began moving thousands of illegal immigrants from a remote island to a top security camp.

Police boats bobbed near the pier at the Tai A Chau island camp as guards herded hundreds of inmates on to special ferries to take them to the Whitehead detention camp in the rural New Territories area, where they will be readied for repatriation.
Reporters watched from a distance from aboard a boat as the first batch of about 200 Vietnamese left their huts and moved peacefully towards the jetty.
A long column of the boatpeople -- including elderly people and entire families of men, women and children -- filed along the jetty clutching bundles of possessions.
Monday was the first day of the transfer from the small island, which lies off the coast of Lantau, the largest isle in the Hong Kong archipelago.
Police say it will take about 10 days, at a rate of 500 or so detainees per day, to clear the island of its 5,500 inmates.

The operation is a crucial phase in a drive to empty the British colony's detention camps through forced and voluntary repatriations before the territory is handed back to China in the middle of next year.
Beijing insists they all be gone by that time.
But Hong Kong is not the only place wiping clean the boatpeople slate. Across Southeast Asia, similar drives have been under way this year to clear the camps and send the migrants back home.
This year, Hong Kong has virtually halved its population of boatpeople to about 12,000 through repatriations.
The detainees are the last of the flood of tens of thousands of Vietnamese who fled their country after the communists won the Vietnam War in 1975.
Police launches escorted the ferry departing from Tai A Chau in case any detainees tried to leap into the sea and escape.
A firefighting boat was also deployed, and paramedic units were landed on the island in case of violence.

On Monday morning, the operation began smoothly with no signs of the violent resistance or self-inflicted injuries that have marked some other mass transfers of Vietnamese illegals in Hong Kong and in nearby countries such as Thailand.
"We hope that by transferring them to Whitehead, more boatpeople will be encouraged to apply for voluntary repatriation," said Security Branch spokesman Mak Kwok-wah.
"The voluntary repatriation level has been very low at Tai A Chau. There were only 170 or so volunteers there last year," he told reporters at the scene.
Whitehead was rocked by fierce rioting in May this year when inmates burned down part of the camp and attempted a mass breakout. The fugitives were quickly rounded up.
Tai A Chau was also hit by a riot in 1989 after the first wave of repatriations, when police had to beat a hasty retreat from the island in the face of overwhelming violence.
